prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map depicts a kitchen scene as the camera wearer turns rightward and steps toward a cooking area across five frames, with no other people present in the room. In frames 1 and 2, wooden upper cabinets sit very close in front of and above the wearer at roughly 0.3 to 0.6 metres (bright white/light grey), partially occluding the lower countertop, plates, and the wearer's extended left arm below at about 0.6 to 0.9 metres. As the wearer turns right in frame 3, a white stove and range hood appear in front at about 0.8 to 1.2 metres, flanked by left countertop bottles within arm's reach (0.6 to 0.9 metres), a right countertop with a plate of food (1.2 to 1.8 metres), a refrigerator further right (2.0 to 2.5 metres), and a dark background kitchen area beyond 3 to 5 metres. In frames 4 and 5, the wearer approaches the stove (brightening to 0.4 to 0.8 metres, well within arm's reach) and then turns slightly right toward the adjacent counter while the left side of the stove becomes partially cropped out of view. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the overhanging upper cabinets and range hood from the recessed backsplash and deep background room, though it is unreliable on thin utensils like the spatula, small bottle details in frame 2 due to motion blur, and the flat countertop in frame 5 where surface items blend into the counter's depth plane.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is completely blank in frames 1 and 2, failing to detect the upper cabinets, countertop items, or the camera wearer's arm and hands located 0.3 to 0.9 metres away, and no other people are present in any frame. In frame 3, as the wearer faces the cooking area, the map detects five small bottles clustered on the left counter at about 0.6 to 0.9 metres (within arm's reach and 0.1 to 0.3 metres from each other) and labels the central white stove (0.8 to 1.2 metres away) as 'oven', while misclassifying the right-hand countertop (1.2 to 1.8 metres away) as a second 'oven'. In frame 4, as the wearer steps closer (0.4 to 0.8 metres from the stove), the stove mask expands across the lower-left and centre within arm's reach, three bottles remain visible on the far left edge before being occluded by the frame boundary, and the right countertop is again mislabelled as 'oven'. By frame 5, as the wearer turns rightward, the bottles are fully out of view on the left, the true stove is partially visible on the lower left at 0.5 to 0.9 metres, and the misclassified right countertop mask sits beside it at 0.8 to 1.5 metres. While the masks help isolate the cluster of small condiment bottles against the busy counter edge in frames 3 and 4 better than a quick glance at the RGB, the map is highly unreliable because it misses all objects in frames 1 and 2, ignores the frying pans, food plate, and upper cabinets, and falsely labels the right countertop as an oven.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all five frames, detecting no body or hand keypoints anywhere in the scene. In the RGB strip, no other people are present to face or look toward the camera wearer, as the scene only contains the kitchen layout with cabinets, countertops, a stove, and cooking utensils ranging from 0.3 metres in the foreground to over 4 metres in the background. However, in frames 1 and 2, the camera wearer's own left forearm and both hands are visible below the upper cabinets at roughly 0.4 to 0.7 metres in front of and below the camera, reaching into the dish area within arm's reach before dropping out of the lower frame boundary in frames 3 through 5. Because the pose estimator outputs no yellow body or magenta hand skeletons at all, it provides no spatial information beyond what is visible in the RGB image and is unreliable for tracking the wearer's ego-hands in frames 1 and 2, where motion blur, steep downward viewing angles, and partial occlusion by the upper cabinet door and lower image edge prevent detection.
